description: E12 case catalog. A case passes only if every listed source passed: JUnit/Playwright results (patterns use PowerShell -like), lab verdict files (value at path must equal expect) and, when grader is true, the independent SQL financial hard gates of every included run. Each case carries the acceptance-matrix dimension it scores; reproducibility is scored from the exact-SHA CI run and the clean-tree flags.

cases.title: Every committed journal balances; amounts are exact NZD minor units; posted history is append-only
Identical idempotency key returns the original receipt; a changed payload under the same key is rejected; a lost response recovers with the original key
Concurrent debits of one hot payer never overdraw; opposing transfers use a deterministic lock order without deadlock
Any failure inside the transfer transaction rolls back journal, postings, projection, receipt and outbox together; crash before commit leaves nothing

cases.category: B Corporate identity and Policy B
cases.title: Executed role x route x object matrix: 12 principals x 44 routes, concealment 404, missing role 403, denied mutations without side effects

cases.category: B Corporate identity and Policy B
cases.title: Maker cannot approve their own payment or payroll even when holding both roles; approval binds the immutable digest and version

cases.category: B Corporate identity and Policy B
cases.title: Generic transfers cannot debit a corporate account; payroll identities cannot be claimed by public transfers

cases.category: B Corporate identity and Policy B
cases.title: Role revocation, member suspension and organization suspension remove authority; admin self-grant is refused; actions are audited

cases.category: B Corporate identity and Policy B
cases.title: State changes without or with a forged CSRF token are rejected; sessions rotate on authentication
500 synthetic employees are paid exactly once with deterministic per-item identity and reconciled balances
Competing executors and batches sharing a payer pay each item once and never overdraw
Worker crash after a failed item rolled back but before its failure was recorded: restart records it once, pays the rest once
Transient and terminal item failures are durable; results cannot be forged, deleted or completed early
Business fact and outbox event commit together; concurrent publishers and dispatchers deliver each event once
Interrupted dispatch: an event persisted before a crash is delivered after restart; expired leases are retried idempotently
Retry exhaustion dead-letters visibly; a governed retry is role-gated, audited and idempotent
Settlement, definitive rejection and accepted/pending outcomes post exactly the journals their persisted outcome justifies
UNKNOWN outcome is resolved by inquiry under the original operation identity and digest; no refund or new identity
Signed callbacks: tampered, missing-header, replayed, reused-id, wrong-digest, colliding, gapped and contradictory callbacks never move money twice
Crash after the callback commit, inside the uncommitted settlement, or before the acknowledgement: the original identity settles exactly once after restart without simulator redelivery
A terminated database session during the settlement leaves durable work that completes it once
Genuinely insufficient reserve: obligation kept, CRITICAL exception, restart, audited replenishment, one governed retry, exactly one settlement
Callbacks lost beyond the simulator's delivery budget are detected and redelivered in order after an authenticated inquiry
Competing workers, a duplicate callback and a direct retry produce exactly one settlement
Simulator crash with an ACCEPTED operation: the bank's inquiry fails and is reported, nothing is assumed; after restart the same operation settles once
Projection drift is detected exactly and repaired from immutable postings only
A terminal external outcome without its local journal is detected while the payment is not COMPLETED, also after restart and without a new callback
Negative fixtures: corrupt payment, journal, payroll and event states are refused by PostgreSQL with valid rows unchanged; recoverable dead work is reported
CRITICAL exceptions close only after an independent recheck; the actor and the recheck are audited; undispatched instructions are reported
Exceptions and Operations views stay inside the tenant
Migrations: fresh install, populated V4/V5/V6/V8/V11 upgrades without rewriting history, V7 and V15 refuse inconsistent history; checksums pinned

Logical backup (pg_dump -Fc) of the bank while a payment is only ACCEPTED, restore into a new database after the live bank settled it, and recovery of the simulator's later callbacks under the original operation identity with no second booking; measured RPO/RTO of this run
cases.limitation: Logical backup and restore of the bank database on one workstation: not PITR, not offsite, not a storage failure. Round 3 E10 holds the only PITR run (one local run, RPO 118.922 s, RTO 670.008 s); it is cited, not re-executed.

cases.title: Real-API Chromium journeys: personal banking, corporate maker/checker settlement, payroll with lost response, UNKNOWN inquiry, exception, concealment, role denial and revocation

Accessibility subset on the real application: on nine screens every interactive control and image has an accessible name in the computed accessibility tree, one main landmark, a level-1 heading, a document language and title, and no duplicate element ids
cases.limitation: Not an axe-core or WCAG conformance audit: colour contrast, complete focus order and real screen-reader behaviour are not assessed. E11 keyboard paths and the 390 px overflow check are cited from Round 3.

cases.title: Alerting: a real Prometheus 3.13.3 scrape fires the owed-effect and reserve-shortfall alerts on a genuinely created shortage (shortfall 30.00 NZD measured) and both resolve after the audited replenishment and one governed retry
cases.limitation: Rule evaluation only; notification delivery (Alertmanager, paging) is out of scope.

cases.title: W3C trace continuity: approval -> instruction dispatch -> simulator request -> callback delivery -> bank callback -> settlement, stitched only through recorded parent ids and links; client trace ids are never authority
cases.limitation: Spans are retained as structured local log records; there is no trace backend or sampling policy.

dimensions.financial: Financial correctness: balanced, exact, once-only money movement and its reconciliation
dimensions.security: Security and authorization: Policy B, maker/checker, tenant concealment, signed callbacks, CSRF
dimensions.async: Asynchronous reliability: durable events, competing workers, retries, stable operation identity
dimensions.recovery: Recovery: process crashes, terminated sessions, reserve shortage, lost callbacks, restarts, restore, migrations
dimensions.observability: Observability: alerts on real failure states, trace continuity
dimensions.fullstack: Full-stack behavior: real-API browser journeys and accessibility
